records.subject: Welcome to Wrenfield, Bright Studio!
records.body:
Hi Tunde,

Your workspace for Bright Studio is ready to go. The single highest-leverage thing in week one is creating a real project rather than a test one -- it's what makes the first week actually useful.

I'm here if anything's unclear.

Best,

decisions.rationale: Six days in with zero product activity: no project, no invite, no milestone. Two outreach emails ([email:3fb54439], [email:0f146df8]) went unanswered and no tickets filed, so there's no signal of engagement. Silent, inactive accounts rarely self-activate in the remaining 8 days.

draft.subject: Getting Bright Studio's first project started
draft.body:
Hi Tunde,

Following up on my note last week — I know early days get busy, so I'll keep this short.

In Wrenfield, projects are the main organizing unit, and tasks live inside them, so a single real project is usually the fastest way to see whether this fits how Bright Studio works. The in-app onboarding flow walks through creating a first project, and teammates can be invited from Account Settings -> Members at any time whenever you're ready to bring the team in.

Would a short call this week help? I'm happy to walk through that first project with you.

Best,
Nadia
